findings.quote: although they had many opportunities and favourable moments, they let them slip, and at times escaped from fears and dangers as well
findings.problem: Greek: πολλὰς μὲν περιστάσεις καὶ καιροὺς ἔχοντες, ἐνίοτε δὲ φόβους καὶ κινδύνους διωλίσθανον. The περιστάσεις and καιροί are critical, dangerous junctures (parallel to φόβους καὶ κινδύνους), not opportunities; διολισθάνω means they slipped through/out of them. English reverses this into missed opportunities.
findings.proposed_fix: although they often found themselves in critical straits and junctures, and at times in fears and dangers, they slipped through

units.note: Also: the 'the one ... the other' for Arcadians/Laconians (τοῦ μὲν ... τοῦ δὲ) follows the Greek's own loose order; the following clause makes clear Sparta is hostile. Left alone.
Lacuna after προσῄει τοῖς ἐφόροις is marked [...] in English; end-of-chapter gap also marked.
